feed.title: Consumer Price Index
feed.subtitle: "The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is a measure of the average change over time in the prices paid by urban consumers for a fixed market basket of goods and services. The CPI is based on the prices of food, clothing, shelter, fuel, drugs, transportation fares, doctors' and dentists' fees, and other goods and services that people buy for day-to-day living. This release is issued monthly. For more information, visit the Consumer Price Indexes home page at www.bls.gov/cpi/. "

entry.title: CPI for all items increases 0.4% in August; gasoline rises
entry.content: In August, the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers rose 0.4 percent, seasonally adjusted (SA), and rose 3.4 percent over the last 12 months, not seasonally adjusted (NSA). The index for all items less food and energy rose 0.3 percent in August (SA), up 2.4 percent over the year (NSA).
